title: Cycle-level pullback compatibility for module cup products

from.place: proof step 3: lift the two input classes to kernel cocycles and compare their paired resolution classes

statement: In the setting of module cohomology on schemes, for a morphism f:X'\to X, quasi-coherent modules F and G, module cup products cup and cup\prime on X and on the tensor-pullbacks, and a cup-paired acyclic resolution D of F and G, the pullback of cup applied to the classes represented by any two cycles of D equals cup\prime applied to the pulled-back classes, after the canonical tensor-pullback comparison on the target.

proof.text: Take computing pairings P,E and additive cochain maps l,r,t with their three class equations and strict pairing equation. The class map of any computing resolution is surjective: cycles project epimorphically onto homology, the computing comparison is an isomorphism, and the injective comparison is an isomorphism. Lift the two given input classes to cycles a0,b0 in P.

Leibniz and the two cycle equations imply that P.pair(a0,b0) is a cycle c0. Transport a0,b0,c0 along l,r,t. The cochain commutation equations preserve the kernel condition; the strict pairing equation says that the transported c0 is the pairing of the transported inputs.

Apply the source IsModuleCupProduct characterization to P and c0, replacing the lifted input classes by the given classes. The target class equation identifies the pullback of this product with the class of transported c0. Apply the target IsModuleCupProduct characterization to E and the transported cycles, then substitute the two input class equations. This gives the asserted equality for the original resolution D.
